methodological_rigor.justification: This is a multicenter retrospective registry analysis (KLASS-13) comparing single-port (spRRDG, n = 86) versus conventional reduced-port (cRRDG, n = 734) robotic distal gastrectomy with defined exclusions (e.g., distant metastasis; R1/R2; non-distal gastrectomy procedures). The design is appropriate for feasibility and short-term perioperative comparisons but is vulnerable to confounding by center/surgeon and by early adoption of the SP platform (noted in the manuscript), and there is no randomization or matching described. The statistical approach primarily uses unadjusted between-group tests (t/Mann–Whitney; chi-square/Fisher) with subgroup analyses by lymphadenectomy extent, with limited detail on how any stated 'adjustment' was performed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an individual multicenter retrospective cohort comparison of surgical approaches, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b. Clinically, it addresses oncologic adequacy (retrieved lymph nodes with explicit ≥16-node threshold) and recovery outcomes (length of stay, first flatus, soft diet initiation) in gastric cancer surgery. While long-term oncologic outcomes are not assessed and the SP group reflects early adoption, the findings are directly relevant to selecting platforms for carefully selected patients.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript explicitly states it is reported in line with STROCSS and provides clear registry provenance (KGCA/KLASS-13), IRB approval with waiver of consent, inclusion/exclusion flow, and defined perioperative and recovery endpoints including Clavien–Dindo complications and lymphadenectomy extent. However, the schema-supported 'standard_used' cannot directly encode STROCSS, and there is no explicit data/code availability statement in the provided text. Confounding control is limited in the described methods (primarily unadjusted comparisons) despite inherent multicenter and learning-curve biases.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript frames this as the first and largest multicenter comparative analysis of single-port versus multi-port reduced-port robotic distal gastrectomy across platforms using a dedicated registry. It contributes new comparative data on lymph node yield and enhanced recovery metrics in a real-world cohort. Novelty is tempered by the short-term outcome horizon and retrospective, early-adoption nature of the SP experience.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is quantitatively specific (operative time, retrieved lymph nodes, and ERAS-related outcomes with p-values) and maintains appropriate caution about limiting SP use to early-stage disease. Methods clearly define REPROG, cohort assembly and exclusions, and the set of outcomes compared. The discussion explicitly acknowledges retrospective multicenter biases and the SP learning-curve limitation.

key_strengths: Large multicenter registry cohort (820 distal gastrectomy cases) with clear exclusions and clinically relevant endpoints including lymph node yield and ERAS-related recovery metrics.
Oncologic adequacy is addressed explicitly via retrieved LN counts and the ≥16-node threshold, with subgroup analyses by D1+ versus D2 lymphadenectomy.
key_concerns: Retrospective, non-randomized comparison with likely center/surgeon and learning-curve confounding; the SP platform is described as early adoption (2022–2023), which can bias operative time and outcomes.
Statistical methods are mainly unadjusted between-group tests; details of any claimed covariate adjustment are not clearly specified in the provided Methods section.
Outcomes are short-term only; long-term oncologic safety and survival are not evaluated.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a strong real-world dataset with clear clinical relevance, but causal inference and generalizability are limited by retrospective early-adoption confounding and the absence of long-term outcomes; it could reach a higher-tier surgical/oncology journal with stronger confounding control and clearer adjusted analyses.
